mainTopic: The opening משנה of מסכת שבת: eight cases of carrying between a private and public domain and who is חייב, plus the גמרא's opening comparison to the 'two that are four' of שבועות.
overview: The משנה opens מסכת שבת with a short rule: יציאות השבת, the acts of carrying between domains, are 'two that are four inside, and two that are four outside.' It then asks כיצד, 'how?', and explains with a poor person (עני) standing in the street and a homeowner (בעל הבית) standing in his house. In four cases one person does the whole act of carrying, picking the object up in one domain and putting it down in the other, and that person is חייב. In four more cases the act is split between the two people, so both are פטור. Together these eight cases fill the count of four inside and four outside. The גמרא then opens by quoting a similar משנה in מסכת שבועות, which also says 'two that are four,' about oaths. This sets up a comparison between the two משניות that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The opening rule: carrying on שבת is 'two that are four'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the basic number of ways to carry between domains: two that are four inside, and two that are four outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The acts of carrying out on שבת are two that are really four inside, and two that are really four outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens מסכת שבת with a short, packed rule about יציאות השבת, the acts of carrying between domains. It counts them as 'two that are four' for the person inside and 'two that are four' for the person outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not explaining yet. It only gives the count. Each 'two' are basic acts that turn into 'four' cases, but we only learn what the cases are in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: the text of the משנה being studied
The acts of 'going out' on שבת, meaning carrying an object from one domain to another
Inside: in the private domain (the house)
Outside: in the public domain (the street)

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
The acts of carrying out on Shabbat
phrases.notes: Literally 'the goings-out.' It means moving an object between a house and the street, in either direction.

phrases.english: are two that are four inside
and two that are four outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְצִיאוֹת הַשַּׁבָּת שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע בִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the מסכת; nothing comes before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The acts of carrying between domains on שבת are counted as two that are four inside and two that are four outside.
steps.whyThisMatters: This short count is the base of the whole first sugya. The גמרא will spend a long time working out what exactly the 'four' cases are.

steps.title: The משנה asks how these cases work
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks 'How?' to start explaining its short rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks itself 'How?' This line prepares the next move, where the משנה will lay out the actual cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. It is a question asking for an explanation. The short rule in step 1 needs real examples, and the next lines will give them.

keyTerms.meaning: How? In what way? A word used to open an explanation

phrases.english: How so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the cases behind the short count given in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What are the actual cases of carrying behind the count 'two that are four'?

steps.title: The poor person does the carrying, so he is liable
steps.stepSummary: The עני stands outside and the בעל הבית stands inside. If the עני reaches in and either puts something into the בעל הבית's hand or takes something out of it, the עני is חייב and the בעל הבית is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The poor man stands outside, and the homeowner stands inside. If the poor man stretched his hand inside and put an object into the homeowner's hand, or took an object from the homeowner's hand and carried it out, the poor man is liable and the homeowner is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers 'How?' with a scene: a poor man in the street and a homeowner in his house. It gives two cases where the poor man does the carrying, and rules that he is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the עני carries in: he brings an object from the street into the house. In the second case he carries out: he takes an object from inside to the street. Either way, he is the one who lifted the object and put it down in the new domain, so only he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person; here, the one standing in the public domain
The homeowner; here, the one standing inside the private domain
Liable: he has broken the law of שבת and is responsible (for example, a קרבן חטאת if it was by mistake)
Exempt: not liable for punishment or a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the בעל הבית is פטור because he is in his own house. He is פטור because he did not do the whole act of carrying. The עני did both the lifting and the putting down.

phrases.english: The poor man stands outside
and the homeowner is inside.
If the poor man stretched his hand inside

phrases.aramaic: וְנָתַן לְתוֹךְ יָדוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: and put an object into the homeowner's hand,
phrases.notes: The object started in the עני's hand out in the street, so this is carrying in.

phrases.english: or he took an object from inside it and carried it out,
phrases.notes: 'From inside it' means from inside the homeowner's hand.

phrases.english: the poor man is liable and the homeowner is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶעָנִי עוֹמֵד בַּחוּץ וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת בִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'How?' of step 2 with the first pair of cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the person outside reaches in and either puts in or takes out an object, he alone is חייב.

steps.title: The homeowner does the carrying, so he is liable
steps.stepSummary: Now the בעל הבית reaches out to the street and either puts something into the עני's hand or takes something from it and brings it in. The בעל הבית is חייב and the עני is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the homeowner stretched his hand outside and put an object into the poor man's hand, or took an object from the poor man's hand and brought it inside, the homeowner is liable and the poor man is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the mirror-image pair of cases. Now the homeowner does the carrying, so he is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the בעל הבית carries out: from his house to the street. In the second he carries in: from the street into his house. The rule stays the same. Whoever does the full act of carrying is חייב, and the other person is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: To the outside: into the public domain
He brought in, carrying from the public domain into the private domain

steps.whatToRemember: In the four cases so far, the one who does the entire act of carrying is חייב, and the other person is פטור. Carrying in and carrying out both count, for the person inside and for the person outside. The next steps add four more cases where the act is split.

phrases.aramaic: פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ לַחוּץ
phrases.english: If the homeowner stretched his hand outside
and put an object into the poor man's hand,
or he took an object from inside it and brought it in,
the homeowner is liable and the poor man is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ לַחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second pair of cases, the mirror image of step 3, with the homeowner as the one carrying.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the person inside reaches out and either puts out or brings in an object, he alone is חייב.

steps.title: Poor man reaches in, both share the act
steps.stepSummary: The עני puts his hand into the house. Either the בעל הבית takes the object out of his hand, or the בעל הבית puts an object into his hand and the עני pulls it out. Both are פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The poor man stretched his hand inside, and the homeowner took something from it. Or the homeowner put something into it and the poor man took it out. Both of them are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues answering its question 'How?' It now gives cases where the עני and the בעל הבית split the carrying between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 3 and 4, one person did the whole job: he picked up the object in one place and put it down in the other. Here the job is split, because one person does the picking up and the other does the putting down. Since nobody did the complete מלאכה alone, both are פטור.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 3. There, the עני did the whole act by himself and was חייב. Here the בעל הבית does half of it, and that is why both are פטור.

phrases.english: The poor man stretched his hand inside
and the homeowner took [an object] from it,
or [the homeowner] put [an object] into it and [the poor man] carried it out
— both of them are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּשַׁט הֶעָנִי אֶת יָדוֹ לִפְנִים וְנָטַל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת מִתּוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same setup as step 3 (the עני reaching in), but now the act is split between two people.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the עני reaches in and the act is shared with the בעל הבית, both are פטור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shared act of carrying makes both people פטור.

steps.title: Homeowner reaches out, both share the act
steps.stepSummary: The בעל הבית puts his hand out to the street. Either the עני takes the object from his hand, or the עני puts an object into his hand and the בעל הבית brings it in. Both are פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The homeowner stretched his hand outside, and the poor man took something from it. Or the poor man put something into it and the homeowner brought it in. Both of them are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the mirror image of step 5. Now the בעל הבית's hand goes outside, and again the act is split between the two people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches step 4 (the בעל הבית reaching out), but there he did the whole act himself and was חייב. Here the עני does either the picking up or the putting down. Because the act is split, both are פטור, just as in step 5.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's full picture: 4 cases where one person does the whole act (that person is חייב), and 4 cases where two people split the act (both are פטור). Together these 8 cases fill the count of 'two that are four inside and two that are four outside,' so the count includes the פטור cases too.
steps.confusionAlert: Here פטור means he is not liable to bring a קרבן חטאת. It does not automatically mean the act is allowed on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ לַחוּץ
phrases.english: The homeowner stretched his hand outside
and the poor man took [an object] from it,
or [the poor man] put [an object] into it and [the homeowner] brought it in
— both of them are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ לַחוּץ וְנָטַל הֶעָנִי מִתּוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror case of step 5, set up like step 4. It completes the משנה's list.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the בעל הבית reaches out and the act is shared with the עני, both are פטור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shared act of carrying makes both people פטור, in either direction.

steps.title: The גמרא opens with a similar משנה about oaths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by quoting a משנה in מסכת שבועות that also says 'two that are four,' this time about oaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned there (in another משנה): Oaths are two that are four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a different משנה that uses the same 'two that are four' wording. This is a setup line: the גמרא is getting ready to compare the two משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said the ways of carrying are 'two that are four.' The משנה in שבועות uses the exact same phrase about oaths. By placing the two side by side, the גמרא prepares to ask why they are worded alike and what the difference between them might be.

keyTerms.meaning: the discussion and analysis that follows the משנה
there, meaning in a different place
oaths, and also the name of a מסכת

steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison is the springboard for the whole opening sugya of מסכת שבת. The גמרא will use it to look into what 'two that are four' means in each place.

phrases.english: Gemara: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means a different משנה, this one in מסכת שבועות.

phrases.english: Oaths: two that are four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the end of the משנה to the start of the גמרא. It picks up the 'two that are four' wording from step 1 and compares it to a parallel משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה in שבועות also counts its cases as 'two that are four.'
